Sam (AE): Hey team -- OrcinPay POC kickoff. They want Redwood Private deployed into their AWS account (multi-AZ), strict egress allowlist, and preservation of client source IPs for downstream logging. Can we confirm architecture options + any pricing delta?
Mira (SE): High level: PrivateLink vs VPC Peering tradeoff. PrivateLink = easier for multi-account / strong isolation, preserves client IP only if using NLB passthrough pattern. Peering preserves IP but needs route table setup and more cross-account routing.
John (NetOps): Peering note: if their onprem path uses a transit GW, source IP can be preserved but we need to ensure SNAT isn't happening at their NAT GW. Also watch for overlap in CIDR ranges.
Paula (OrionPay Admin): Quick Q: they require no internet egress from our private nodes except to Redwood control plane and model fetch endpoints. Is that doable?
Mira (SE): Yes. We can restrict egress to specific FQDNs/IPs. For control plane connectivity we need outbound to: 52.14.23.0/24 (example) and api.redwood-inference.com:443. We'll provide final allowlist.
Anna (Security): Also need answers for the security questionnaire: can you confirm TLS termination location, key management, and whether logs contain customer data?
Liz (Eng): TLS: we terminate TLS at the customer NLB (recommended) for PrivateLink passthrough; for peering deployments customers may choose to terminate at their edge. KMS: customer-managed CMKs supported for Private deployments. Logs: request/latency traces may include prompt metadata; we'll provide scrub/PII guidance and configurable retention.
Sam (AE): Pricing ask from procurement: will there be an incremental fee for PrivateLink vs peering, and for multi-AZ HA?
Mira (SE): Pricing: PrivateLink adds endpoint setup and slightly higher network egress in our quoting model; multi-AZ HA requires reserved capacity or dedicated pods -> monthly commit. I'll pull numbers.
John (NetOps): Firewall snippet for their Ops team, basic egress allowlist (they asked for concrete rules):
```
# outbound from private nodes
TCP 443 -> api.redwood-inference.com (control plane & model sync)
TCP 443 -> s3.amazonaws.com (model artifacts)
UDP 123 -> 169.254.169.123 (NTP/proxy)
TCP 22 -> (optional bastion IPs)
ICMP -> allowed for health checks if they want
```
Paula (OrionPay Admin): That helps. For PrivateLink we need an interface endpoint in our VPC; do we need route changes?
Mira (SE): No route table edits for interface endpoints; you need security group rules to allow inbound from our endpoint ENIs to your NLB/listener. For peering you must add routes and potentially update TGW attachments.
Anna (Security): Please attach the redacted answers for the questionnaire, but short answers OK. Also: SOC2 scope note for Private deploy?
Liz (Eng): Private deployments fall under our enterprise compliance package; SOC2 evidence available under NDA. We'll have Customer Success send the onboarding checklist.
Sam (AE): Action items I got: Mira to provide exact allowlist CIDRs + estimated pricing delta; Liz to confirm KMS/legal SOC2 pointer; John to sanity-check firewall snippet for TGW setups; Anna to confirm questionnaire minimal answers.
Mira (SE): I'll drop the allowlist + a short runbook by EOD. :thumbsup:
John (NetOps): One more gotcha: if they want client-srcip preserved to their downstream logging through our NLB, they must use the TLS passthrough listener and not have an ALB that terminates TLS. Confirmed.
Paula (OrionPay Admin): OK thanks. We'll validate with our net team tomorrow and share their NAT/Transit topology.
deploy-bot: Deployment note: created placeholder ticket DEPL-4221 for OrcinPay private-poc; assign to Mira + John.
Sam (AE): Perfect. I'll loop procurement and book a technical session with their netops for tomorrow.
Paula (OrionPay Admin): Prefer 11am PST.
